eli: heads up — we're seeing a weird scale-in loop in us-west1-gpu last hour. nodes spin up for pending gpu pods then get drained within ~2m because kube-probe failures mark pods not-ready and CA thinks they're evictable. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/LLm/gpu-cluster?orgId=1

priya: ugh. do we have any examples of pods stuck on hostPort or with local storage? those block eviction and confuse CA sometimes

eli: quick grep shows a few image-processor pods using hostPort and one legacy prometheus sidecar with emptyDir. mostly short lived but coincides with scale events.

sasha: my two cents — CA treats nodes as underutilized if pods are `evictable`. If probes fail, pods can flip state and CA may think they are safe to evict. we should tighten scale-down windows and avoid immediate eviction on flaky probes.

kevin: agreed. what flags are folks thinking? iirc we previously set aggressive values to reduce cost.

sasha: proposal for canary cluster:
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m  # current is 2m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=20m # stop evaporating just-added nodes
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
```
That combination prevents CA from instantly considering freshly added GPU nodes unneeded and avoids evicting pods with local storage.

priya: also enable `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5`? some of these nodes are only 40% utilized but evicting increases churn and cost.

eli: +1 on utilization threshold. can we also surface kubelet probe flaps in alerts? i'm seeing CNI intermittent drops that line up with the pod NotReady spikes.

kevin: i'll open an alert to tie `kube_pod_container_status_ready` flapping to node churn. in the medium-term we should: 1) move hostPort services behind a LB, 2) stop sidecars with emptyDir on gpu nodes, 3) add anti-affinity to batch jobs.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: autoscaler config change request submitted by @kevin for canary-us-west1 at 2025-11-03T15:43Z — job/ca-config-canary

sasha: tiny caution — `--expander=least-waste` can over-consolidate across AZs if groups differ. keep `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` so it tries to even distribution. also consider `--max-empty-bulk-delete=1` to slow deleting many empty nodes at once.

priya: test plan: apply flags in canary, run 6-hour soak with synthetic batch load (hostPort + normal gpu pods) and check churn, cost, and P50 latency. rollback if churn > baseline or P50 increases >5%.

eli: i've added the soak job to ci/infra/gpu-soak and linked to the dashboard. will watch during PST morning spike. thanks folks :thumbsup:

kevin: action items summarized:
- kevin: apply canary flag set and enable temp alert for probe flaps
- sasha: validate expander + balance config in simulator (run with current nodepool mixes)
- priya: audit hostPort/emptyDir on gpu node selectors, propose migrations
- eli: monitor soak and collect traces for pod readiness failures

eli: tagging @sasha @priya @kevin — ping me if you need quick access to the canary cluster creds.

sasha: noted. i can run the sim today.

priya: will start the audit, should have a short list by EOD.
